feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is stated for it. The candidate is the iteration 10 design (sensors at x = ±0.030 m with 16 mm footprints, kp 6.0, kd 0.6, ki 0.05, base_speed 1.2, last_direction), the best raced configuration so far at 125.48. Its geometry and controller match iteration 10 field for field, so it is valid and well supported by the evidence. Iteration 10 showed that lowering base_speed from 1.4 to 1.2 raised the total score and s-bend progress (0.24 to 0.34), while oval progress fell (0.57 to 0.51). Iteration 9 showed that widening the sensors to ±0.040 m and raising kp to 8.0 cut progress on both tracks, so that change is not carried forward. Oval max_error has stayed at 0.061 to 0.065 across gains, kd values and sensor reach, so the 0.06 m off-track limit has not been cleared by any tested lever. This is the final iteration, with no later iteration to learn from. Revising now would risk a design that has not been measured, and a delivered design is required to avoid a zero. The best-supported option is to race this design unchanged. Telemetry from the race will still be recorded for the team.
requested_changes: No further change for this final race: race the iteration 10 design unchanged (base_speed 1.2, kp 6.0, kd 0.6, ki 0.05, sensors at x = ±0.030 m, 16 mm, last_direction), because it is the best measured design and the final race needs a delivered candidate.

For the record, if the team later reviews these results: test base_speed between 1.2 and 1.4 and line_loss search_left or search_right, since iteration 10 showed speed trades oval progress against s-bend progress, and line losses at bend entries (1.0 to 1.7 per run) remain the next limit.
